title: Flash-Loaned Governance Vote
summary: Governance counts a voter's CURRENT token balance as voting power. An attacker flash-borrows enough tokens for one transaction, votes a self-serving proposal past quorum, executes it to drain the treasury, and repays the loan — all atomically.
web2Analog: Granting authority based on an instantaneous, attacker-inflatable metric rather than a committed/snapshotted state — the governance analogue of trusting a spot balance.

identify.question: Why can a flash loan capture the vote?
options: vote() uses the caller's current token balance, which a flash loan can inflate for one transaction
identify.explanation: vote() does `votes += govToken.balanceOf(msg.sender)` at call time. A flash loan gives the attacker an enormous balance for the duration of one transaction, so they can single-handedly meet quorum, then repay.

hints: What determines voting power in vote(), and when is it measured?
A flash loan lets you hold a huge balance for exactly one transaction — long enough to vote and execute.
Inside onFlashLoan(): vote(proposalId), then execute(proposalId), before repaying.
The fix snapshots voting power at proposal-creation time (checkpointed balances), so a transient flash-loaned balance carries no weight.

fix.recommendedFix: Never derive voting power from a live balance. Snapshot balances at proposal creation (e.g. ERC20Votes / ERC20Snapshot checkpoints) so only tokens held before the proposal existed can vote, and/or require tokens to be locked for the voting period. A flash loan can mint transient balance for one transaction, so spot balanceOf must never gate governance.
